title: Astrid and the Winter
premise: Folklorist Noor Voss returns to the snowbound village of Haldenmark to record its winter songs, only to find that every photograph from his grandmother's house now contains an extra empty chair—and the villagers refuse to sing any song twice. As he digs into the founders' harvest ritual, Noor learns the chair belongs to Astrid, a founder's daughter erased from records because she was bound into the village's protective rite and never released. The noises he has spent ten years rationalizing are her, still waiting for someone to finish what was started. To survive the rising harvest moon, Noor must choose between completing the ritual—which will bind him in Astrid's place—or breaking it, which frees her but leaves the village exposed to the thing the founders caged beneath the ice. He breaks it, and the village must finally sing the songs twice.
about_author: Gideon Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in remote northern settlements before turning to fiction. Their work draws on half-heard songs, mislabeled photographs, and the quiet horror of communities that agree not to remember.

chapters.title: The House That Counts Wrong
chapters.summary: Noor Voss arrives in Haldenmark after his grandmother's death, cataloguing her house for sale. In every family photograph, an extra wooden chair sits at the edge of frame—older photos too. POV: Noor. Beat: unease disguised as grief; the rational explanations begin to fail.

chapters.title: Songs You Don't Sing Twice
chapters.summary: At the village tavern, Noor records elder Marta Brenner singing a harvest lullaby. When he asks her to repeat a verse, the room goes silent; Marta leaves without a word. The bartender warns him: some songs are sung once so 'she' hears them only once. POV: Noor. Beat: first open confirmation that the village shares a secret.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: ten years earlier, young Noor heard scraping under the floorboards of grandma's house and told himself it was pipes, then mice, then memory. Present-day Noor unpacks his old field recordings and finds the same rhythm underneath every tape. POV: Noor (dual timeline). Beat: the cost of chosen blindness.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the parish archive, Noor finds the 1843 founders' ledger with pages razored out—except for one surviving line: 'the seventh seat shall remain occupied until the moon is full and the debt is paid.' Seven chairs were built for the founding families. POV: Noor. Beat: inheritance as obligation; the mystery gains structure.

chapters.title: Astrid
chapters.summary: A scrap of embroidery names Astrid Lindqvist, daughter of the seventh founder, absent from every census after 1844. The schoolteacher, Ilse, admits offhandedly that children still dare each other to say her name aloud at the well. POV: Noor. Beat: the erased girl becomes real; sympathy replaces fear.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: Noor follows the scraping sound to the root cellar and finds a hatch sealed with iron bands and wax, warm to the touch despite the frost. Through the boards: breathing, patient and slow. He reseals it and tells himself nothing. POV: Noor. Beat: dread made physical; denial's last stand.

chapters.title: The Council of Quiet Men
chapters.summary: Village head Eirik Halvorsen summons Noor and offers him money to leave before the thaw road closes. He explains nothing except this: 'Your grandmother kept her end. The house chose you anyway.' POV: Noor, with Eirik's controlled menace. Beat: power revealed—the village governs by silence and payment.

chapters.title: Marta's Confession
chapters.summary: Marta, drunk on aquavit, tells Noor the songs aren't folk music—they're a leash. Each verse sung once renews the binding; singing twice would answer Astrid, and answering means the ritual must be finished or broken. Her own sister finished it in 1971. She never came back. POV: Marta. Beat: loyalty vs. truth crystallizes; the rules are finally named.

chapters.title: Photographs of the Empty Year
chapters.summary: Noor studies grandma's albums and realizes the extra chair appears in photos dated after 1971—after the last attempt. Grandma knew. A letter falls from the album's spine: 'If you're reading this, finish it kindly. She was only ever a girl.' POV: Noor. Beat: grief reframed as complicity; the family inheritance is the debt itself.

chapters.title: Ilse Breaks Rank
chapters.summary: Schoolteacher Ilse secretly gives Noor the razored ledger pages she stole years ago: the full ritual, requiring seven voices, seven seats, and a willing heir of the seventh line. Noor is the last of the Lindqvist blood. POV: Ilse. Beat: an ally gained; the stakes become personal and inescapable.

chapters.title: The Thing Beneath the Wax
chapters.summary: The hatch breaks open in the night. What emerges isn't Astrid—it's what the founders fed her to, a hunger wearing the shape of winter itself, held at bay only because Astrid's presence confuses it. Noor survives by standing inside a ring of salt and song. POV: Noor. Beat: terror escalates; the true enemy is revealed.

chapters.title: Eirik's Bargain
chapters.summary: Eirik admits the truth: the council has been feeding the ritual substitutes for decades—drifters, the desperate, once Marta's sister. They want Noor bound in Astrid's place because a willing heir holds longer. He offers Noor his grandmother's house and a lie of a life. POV: Eirik. Beat: power's corruption laid bare; the villain believes himself a shepherd.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Marta recants, begging Noor to take the binding rather than break it—the village's children, her grandchildren, are all she has. Noor must weigh strangers' safety against a stolen girl's century of captivity. POV: Marta. Beat: the theme's sharpest turn; both choices cost something irreparable.

chapters.title: The Well at Night
chapters.summary: Noor descends the dry well shaft beneath the cellar and finds Astrid's original binding site: a child's chair, a rotted ribbon, and carved words—'I am the seat, I am the song.' For the first time, something answers when he speaks her name. POV: Noor. Beat: contact made; fear becomes compassion.

chapters.title: Astrid Speaks
chapters.summary: Through frost-breath and borrowed dreams, Astrid tells her story: her father bound her willingly to save the village from the famine-winter, promising to release her at the next full harvest moon. He died instead, and the village chose the harvest over the girl, every year since. POV: Astrid. Beat: the heart of the book; the monster was made, not born.

chapters.title: The Council Moves First
chapters.summary: Eirik's men seize Noor's recordings, burn Ilse's ledger pages, and lock him in the church cold-room until the moon rises—they'll drag him to the seats themselves. Ilse frees him but is caught doing it. POV: Noor. Beat: darkest hour; allies pay the price of truth.

chapters.title: Seven Chairs, Six Voices
chapters.summary: On harvest moon eve, the council begins the ritual early with six conscripted singers, planning to force Noor into the seventh seat. But the songs falter—the binding rejects unwilling voices, and the hunger beneath the ice starts to wake. POV: Noor, escaping toward the churchyard. Beat: the villains' machinery fails; chaos looms.

chapters.title: The Song Sung Twice
chapters.summary: Noor reaches the seven chairs and does the forbidden thing: he sings the harvest lullaby twice, aloud, complete. The village freezes. Astrid steps out of the extra chair—solid, young, furious and weeping—as the hunger surges toward the unprotected village. POV: Noor. Beat: climax begins; the choice is made and irreversible.

chapters.title: What the Moon Witnesses
chapters.summary: Astrid refuses to simply flee: she offers herself back to the seat voluntarily—but on new terms, as a willing guardian rather than a prisoner, if the village sings to her twice every year and remembers her name. Noor adds the seventh voice. The hunger is turned back—not destroyed, but bargained with honestly for the first time. POV: alternating Noor/Astrid. Beat: climax resolves through agency, not sacrifice.

chapters.title: Aftermath of the Thaw
chapters.summary: Eirik resigns in disgrace; the council is dissolved and replaced by an open assembly where Marta testifies to everything, including her sister. Ilse recovers. The extra chair remains in every photograph—but now people wave at it. POV: Noor. Beat: accountability and mourning; the village chooses truth over comfort.

chapters.title: The Folklorist's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Noor must decide whether to publish his recordings and research, knowing exposure could bring outsiders, skeptics, and worse to Haldenmark. He publishes the songs but not the mechanism—truth preserved, weapon withheld—and dedicates the book to Astrid Lindqvist, seventh daughter. POV: Noor. Beat: loyalty and truth reconciled imperfectly; the theme lands.

chapters.title: Coda: The Second Verse
chapters.summary: One year later, at the harvest festival, the whole village sings the lullaby twice, faces turned toward the extra chair set at the table's head. Noor stays. Under the floorboards, the sound is no longer scraping—it's humming along. POV: Noor. Beat: resolution with a shiver; peace that must be renewed, annually, together.
